newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia grants more cash for company investment.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia grants more cash for company investment.

text.p: Slovenia's Development Fund will grant a further 1.2 billion tolars ($8.6 million) in loans to local companies to bolster their investment efforts, fund officials said on Friday.
Officials of the Development Fund, set up to aid Slovenia's economic restructuring, said less than half the amount of cash originally offered to firms had been taken up so far.
"Less than 50 percent of the total amount offered has been spent so far and I hope we will be able to grant the rest very soon," fund director Valter Nemec told a news conference.

In November 1995, the fund introduced loans for investment projects to local companies in an effort to create jobs, increase production and strengthen new and existing products. The total amount offered was two billion tolars.
"I ask myself do we really have so few firms with good development and investment ideas?" Nemec said.
The fund had so far received 85 applications for the loans. Only 10 were approved, 34 refused and 31 withdrawn, while a further 10 are still being processed.
"The most problematic condition the firms have to fulfil to get the loan is that they have to be privatised," Nemec said, explaining the reason for the number of rejected applications.
By mid-October, 740 companies had been privatised, with more than 1,200 others in the process of privatisation. -- Novica Mihajlovic, Ljubljana newsroom, 386-61-125-8439
